paragraphs: We are a fully integrated commercial-stage innovative oncology company with an approved next-generation programmed death receptor-1 ("PD-1") inhibitor, LOQTORZI® (toripalimab-tpzi), and a pipeline that includes two mid-stage clinical candidates targeting liver, head and neck, colorectal and other cancers. Our strategy is to grow sales of LOQTORZI in nasopharyngeal carcinoma ("NPC") and advance the development of new indications for LOQTORZI in combination with both our pipeline candidates as well as our partners, driving sales multiples and synergies from proprietary combinations. On May 29, 2025, we changed our corporate name from "Coherus BioSciences, Inc." to "Coherus Oncology, Inc." to better align with our exclusive focus on proprietary innovative immuno-oncology medicines following the completion of the recent divestitures of our biosimilar businesses.

On October 27, 2023, we announced that LOQTORZI was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration ("FDA") in combination with cisplatin and gemcitabine for the first-line treatment of adults with metastatic or recurrent locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and as monotherapy for the treatment of adults with recurrent unresectable, or metastatic NPC with disease progression on or after platinum-containing chemotherapy. LOQTORZI is an anti-PD-1 antibody that we developed in collaboration with Junshi Biosciences Co., Ltd. ("Junshi Biosciences") that is currently the only immune checkpoint inhibitor approved by the FDA for the treatment of these indications that is commercially available in the United States. We announced the launch of LOQTORZI in the U.S. on January 2, 2024. Further evaluation of LOQTORZI is expected through multiple current and planned clinical studies by us, Junshi Biosciences and our biopharma partners.

Our pipeline comprises two mid-stage clinical candidates aimed at overcoming immune resistance in cancer. We plan to develop each of them in combination with LOQTORZI as well as in partnership with other companies with immune activating or cancer agents. Our clinical stage product candidate casdozokitug (CHS-388, formerly SRF388) is an investigational antagonist antibody targeting IL-27, an immune regulatory cytokine, that is overexpressed in certain cancers, including hepatocellular, lung and renal cell carcinoma. Casdozokitug received orphan drug designation from the FDA for the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma ("HCC") in October 2020. The lead indication for casdozokitug is 1L HCC, and it is currently being studied in a randomized Phase 2 study in HCC evaluating casdozokitug in combination with toripalimab and bevacizumab (clinicaltrials.gov identifier# NCT06679985).

Our second clinical-stage product candidate, tagmokitug (CHS-114, formerly SRF114), is an investigational afucosylated IgG1 antibody targeting CCR8, a chemokine receptor highly expressed on regulatory T cells ("Treg cells") in the tumor microenvironment ("TME"). We are enrolling patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma ("HNSCC") in the U.S. in a clinical trial evaluating safety and pharmacokinetics of tagmokitug with and without LOQTORZI (clinicaltrials.gov identifier# NCT05635643). We have also initiated a multiregional Phase 1b clinical study of tagmokitug in combination with toripalimab and/or other treatments in participants with advanced solid tumors including several cohorts including 2L upper GI adenocarcinoma, 2L esophageal squamous cell carcinoma ("ESCC"), 1LESCC, and Phase 2a cohort evaluating 4L+ colorectal cancer (clinicaltrials.gov identifier# NCT06657144). We have planned a clinical study evaluating tagmokitug in combination with pasritamig (a T cell engaging bispecific antibody targeting KLK2) in metastatic castrate resistant prostate cancer.
Coherus is executing a coordinated initiative to onshore the biomanufacturing process for LOQTORZI, casdozokitug and tagmokitug to the United States.

We have scientific expertise, manufacturing capabilities, and U.S.-based experience across oncology clinical development, regulatory affairs, sales, and medical affairs, which have supported the commercialization of LOQTORZI. We expect to leverage these capabilities as we continue to advance our immuno-oncology franchise.
We commercialize LOQTORZI in the United States, and we have global rights to develop and commercialize casdozokitug and tagmokitug.
Our portfolio includes the following product and product candidates:

● LOQTORZI was developed for its ability to block PD-1 interactions with its ligands, PD-L1 and PD-L2, by binding to the FG loop on the PD-1 receptor. We believe blocking PD-1 interactions with PD-L1 and PD-L2 can help to promote the immune system's

ability to attack and kill tumor cells. On October 27, 2023, we announced that LOQTORZI was approved by the FDA in combination with cisplatin and gemcitabine for the first-line treatment of adults with metastatic or recurrent locally advanced NPC, and as monotherapy for the treatment of adults with recurrent, unresectable, or metastatic NPC with disease progression on or after platinum-containing chemotherapy. LOQTORZI is an anti-PD-1 antibody that we developed in collaboration with Junshi Biosciences. We announced the launch of LOQTORZI in the U.S. on January 2, 2024.

On December 11, 2023 we announced that NCCN updated the clinical practice guidelines for NPC to include LOQTORZI as a preferred, category 1 first-line treatment option for adults with metastatic or recurrent locally advanced NPC when used in combination with cisplatin and gemcitabine. On November 26, 2024, NCCN made a further update to the clinical practice guidelines for NPC to specify that LOQTORZI is the only preferred category 1 first-line treatment option for adults with metastatic or recurrent locally advanced NPC when used in combination with cisplatin and gemcitabine. The guidelines also recommend LOQTORZI monotherapy as the only preferred treatment in subsequent lines of therapy with disease progression on or after a platinum-containing therapy.

Further evaluation of LOQTORZI is expected through multiple current and planned clinical studies by us and our partners. We have a post marketing commitment study active and enrolling patients in locations in the U.S. and Canada in order to further evaluate the safety and efficacy of toripalimab in combination with chemotherapy (cisplatin and gemcitabine) in patients with advanced NPC (clinicaltrials.gov identifier# NCT06457503). Junshi Biosciences has an active multiregional Phase 3 clinical study evaluating the treatment of LOQTORZI with its investigational anti-BTLA antibody in LS-SCLC (clinicaltrials.gov identifier# NCT06095583). INOVIO Pharmaceuticals, Inc. plans a randomized Phase 3 study of INO-3112 and toripalimab in locally advanced, high risk HPV16/18+ oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. Cancer Research Institute is evaluating toripalimab in combination with ENB Therapeutics' investigational agent ENB-003 in its Phase 2 trial titled, "Immunotherapy Platform Study in Platinum Resistant High Grade Serous Ovarian Cancer (IPROC)" (clinicaltrials.gov identifier# NCT04918186) that is being performed in collaboration with Canadian Cancer Trials Group. STORM Therapeutics, Ltd. is evaluating its METTL3 inhibitor STC-15 in combination with LOQTORZI in a Phase 1b/2 study (clinicaltrials.gov identifier# NCT06975293) for the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, melanoma, and endometrial cancer. On June 27, 2024, we entered into a license Agreement with Apotex, Inc. ("Apotex"), pursuant to which, we granted to Apotex an exclusive license under our rights to toripalimab to commercialize toripalimab within Canada ("Canada License Agreement"). On October 23, 2025, Health Canada approved LOQTORZI for the treatment of recurrent unresectable or metastatic NPC.

● Casdozokitug (CHS-388, formerly SRF388), is an investigational recombinant human IgG1 monoclonal antibody targeting IL-27, an immune regulatory cytokine, or protein that is overexpressed in certain cancers, including hepatocellular, lung and renal cell carcinoma. IL-27 is a cytokine secreted by macrophages and antigen presenting cells that plays an important physiological role in suppressing the immune system, as evidenced by its ability to resolve tissue inflammation. In addition, IL-27 is highly expressed during pregnancy and its expression is correlated with maternal-fetal tolerance. Due to its immune regulatory nature, there is a rationale for inhibiting IL-27 to treat cancer, as this approach will influence the activity of multiple types of immune cells that are necessary to recognize and attack a tumor. Casdozokitug received orphan drug designation from the FDA for the treatment of HCC in October 2020. Casdozokitug is currently being evaluated in an ongoing randomized Phase 2 clinical study in HCC evaluating casdozokitug in combination with toripalimab and bevacizumab (clinicaltrials.gov identifier# NCT06679985).

● Tagmokitug (CHS-114, formerly SRF114), is an investigational human afucosylated IgG1 monoclonal antibody selectively targeting CCR8, a chemokine receptor highly expressed on regulatory T cells ("Treg cells") in the tumor microenvironment. Tagmokitug is designed as a cytolytic antibody to cause depletion of intra-tumoral Treg cells, important regulators of immune suppression and tolerance, through antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity ("ADCC"), or antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis ("ADCP"), or both. Tagmokitug has shown anti-tumor activity as monotherapy and in combination with anti-PD-1 antibodies in preclinical models. We are currently evaluating tagmokitug in combination with toripalimab in a Phase 1b clinical study in second-line HNSCC (clinicaltrials.gov identifier# NCT05635643). We also have an ongoing Phase 1b/2a clinical study of tagmokitug in combination with toripalimab and/or other treatments in participants with advanced solid tumors with the first cohorts evaluating upper GI adenocarcinoma, esophageal squamous cell cancer and microsatellite stable ("MSS") colorectal cancer (clinicaltrials.gov identifier# NCT06657144).

headings: Risks Related to Our Financial Condition and Capital Requirements
Risks Related to Launch and Commercialization of our Product and our Product Candidates
We have a limited operating history in an emerging regulatory environment on which to assess our business.
Our product and our product candidates, even if approved, will remain subject to regulatory scrutiny.
Any product candidates for which we intend to seek approval as original biologic products may face competition sooner than anticipated.
Risks Related to Our Ability to Hire and Retain Highly Qualified Personnel

We may experience difficulties in managing changes in our number of employees, particularly due to employees departing due to divestitures, reductions in force and turnover, which could disrupt our operations.
Risks Related to Reliance on Third Parties
We are dependent on Junshi Biosciences for the commercialization of our product and the failure to commercialize could have a material adverse effect on our business and operating results.
Risks Related to Our Future Operations Following the UDENYCA Sale
There is no guarantee that we will receive either of the Earnout Payments under the UDENYCA Purchase Agreement.

There are risks and uncertainties associated with the UDENYCA TSA, one or more of which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows or stock price.

paragraphs: Investing in the common stock of a commercial-stage innovative oncology company, including one with a significant international partnership and multiple product candidates in development, is a highly speculative undertaking and involves a substantial degree of risk. You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below, together with all of the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. If any of the following risks are realized, our business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects could be materially and adversely affected. The risks described below are not the only risks facing us. Risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently deem to be immaterial also may materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and/or prospects.

We have a limited history of profitability, which we have not maintained and may not achieve again, and only one product that has been approved and marketed and with multiple product candidates that are not approved and still in development.

We have generated significant operating losses in all the years since our inception except for certain periods that had gains from divestitures and 2020 and 2019. It is uncertain that we will be profitable in future periods, particularly now that the UDENYCA Sale was consummated, as research and development is expensive and risky. The amount of our future net losses or any future net income will depend, in part, on the amount of our future expenditures offset by the amount of future product sales, including sales of our current product or any other products that may receive regulatory approval. Innovative oncology product development is a highly speculative undertaking and involves a substantial degree of risk.

For example, as of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $1.4 billion. The losses and accumulated deficit were primarily due to the substantial investments we made to commercialize our product and identify, develop or acquire our product candidates, including conducting, among other things, analytical characterization, process development and manufacturing, formulation and clinical studies and providing general and administrative support for these operations.

We have incurred and anticipate we will continue to incur certain development and commercial expenses for LOQTORZI, the anti-PD-1 antibody we licensed from Junshi Biosciences in 2021, and have agreed to pay up to $90.0 million for the achievement of certain regulatory approvals and up to $290.0 million for the attainment of certain sales thresholds. The launch of this product and future work to advance our other product candidates through clinical development in combination with toripalimab will be expensive and could result in us continuing to experience future net losses.

For LOQTORZI, our only commercial product, and if we obtain regulatory approval to market any other product candidate, our future revenue will depend upon the size of any markets in which our product candidates may receive approval and our ability to achieve sufficient market acceptance, pricing, reimbursement from third-party payers, and adequate market share for our product candidates which include all product candidates for which we obtained commercial rights, in those markets. However, even if additional product candidates in addition to our current product gain regulatory approval and are commercialized, we may not become profitable.

As a result, the assets, liabilities, and results of the biosimilar businesses were classified to discontinued operations in our Form 10-K herein. As such, we have retrospectively reclassified all assets, liabilities, and results of the biosimilar businesses as discontinued operations in the following discussion and adjusted all references to the assets, liabilities, and results of our biosimilar businesses accordingly.

We are a fully integrated commercial-stage innovative oncology company with an approved next-generation programmed death receptor-1 inhibitor, LOQTORZI® (toripalimab-tpzi), and a pipeline that includes two mid-stage clinical candidates targeting liver, head and neck, colorectal and other cancers. Our strategy is to grow sales of LOQTORZI in NPC and advance the development of new indications for LOQTORZI in combination with both our pipeline candidates as well as our partners, driving sales multiples and synergies from proprietary combinations. On May 29, 2025, we changed our corporate name from "Coherus BioSciences, Inc." to "Coherus Oncology, Inc." to better align with our exclusive focus on proprietary innovative immuno-oncology medicines following the completion of the recent divestitures of our biosimilar businesses and the transition to an exclusive focus on overcoming immune resistance in cancer with novel drugs.

We previously owned UDENYCA (pegfilgrastim-cbqv), which was launched commercially in a pre-filled syringe presentation in the United States in January 2019, followed by the launch of UDENYCA in an autoinjector presentation in May 2023 and the launch of UDENYCA ONBODY in February 2024. On December 2, 2024, we entered into the UDENYCA Purchase Agreement, pursuant to which the Company agreed to divest the UDENYCA Business to Intas. On April 11, 2025, we completed the divestiture of the UDENYCA Business to Intas for upfront, all-cash consideration of $483.4 million, inclusive of $118.4 million for UDENYCA product inventory. Intas has designated Accord to purchase the physical assets, including product inventory. We are eligible to receive two additional payments of $37.5 million each (together, the "Earnout Payments"). The first such payment is payable by Intas to us if net sales (as defined in the UDENYCA Purchase Agreement, "Net Sales") of UDENYCA for four consecutive fiscal quarters from July 1, 2025 through September 30, 2026 are equal to or greater than $300 million, and the second such payment is payable by Intas to us if Net Sales of UDENYCA for four consecutive fiscal quarters from July 1, 2025 through March 31, 2027 are equal to or greater than $350 million.

The UDENYCA Sale represented the last and most significant divestiture of our biosimilar businesses, which comprised the UDENYCA, YUSIMRY and CIMERLI franchises; therefore, the strategic shift criteria had been met and discontinued operations presentation has been included in the consolidated financial statements for all periods presented.

We have a depth of scientific expertise, an experienced and robust manufacturing know-how and oncology clinical, regulatory, market access, sales, key account management and medical affairs capabilities in the United States, which has supported the commercialization of LOQTORZI. We expect to further leverage these capabilities as we continue to advance our immuno-oncology franchise.
We primarily operate in the United States and partner with companies that operate in other countries.

On December 2, 2024, we entered into the UDENYCA Purchase Agreement by and between us and Intas. Pursuant to the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the UDENYCA Purchase Agreement, we agreed to divest the UDENYCA Business to Intas for $483.4 million in cash, inclusive of $118.4 million of UDENYCA product inventory, subject to downward adjustment by the amount of inventory delivered at the closing of the UDENYCA Sale less than the Inventory Target. In addition, we are also eligible to receive two additional Earnout Payments of $37.5 million each, provided that certain minimum UDENYCA Net Sales thresholds are met during specified periods after the closing of the UDENYCA Sale. The first such payment is payable by Intas to us if net sales of UDENYCA for four consecutive fiscal quarters within the first five full fiscal quarters following the consummation of the UDENYCA Sale are equal to or greater than $300 million, and the second such payment is payable by Intas to us if net sales of UDENYCA for four consecutive fiscal quarters within the first seven full fiscal quarters following the consummation of the UDENYCA Sale are equal to or greater than $350 million.

Our board of directors unanimously approved and declared the UDENYCA Purchase Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereby, including the UDENYCA Sale, to be in the best interest of the Company and its stockholders, and resolved to recommend that the our stockholders adopt the UDENYCA Purchase Agreement. There was a vote of our stockholders at a special stockholder meeting on March 11, 2025 where our stockholders approved the UDENYCA Sale, the UDENYCA Purchase Agreement and the other transactions and ancillary documents contemplated by the Asset Purchase Agreement. paragraphs: 本公司為一家完整整合的商業階段創新腫瘤學公司，已取得核准的下一代程式死亡受體-1（"PD-1"）抑制劑LOQTORZI®（toripalimab-tpzi），並擁有包含兩項中階段臨牀候選藥物的產品線，目標為肝臟、頭頸部、結腸直腸及其他癌症。本公司策略為在鼻咽癌（"NPC"）領域擴大LOQTORZI的銷售，並推進LOQTORZI在與本公司產品線候選藥物及合作夥伴藥物組合的新適應症開發，以驅動自有組合的銷售倍數與協同效益。於2025年5月29日，本公司將公司名稱由"Coherus BioSciences, Inc."更名為"Coherus Oncology, Inc."，以更符合本公司專注於自有創新免疫腫瘤學藥物的獨家重點，並在完成近期生物相似藥業務資產處置後。

於2023年10月27日，本公司宣佈LOQTORZI已獲美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）核准，與順鉑及吉西他濱組合用於治療成人轉移性或復發性局部晚期鼻咽癌的一線治療，並作為單藥用於治療成人復發性不可切除或轉移性鼻咽癌，且在含鉑化療後疾病進展的患者。LOQTORZI為本公司與 Junshi Biosciences Co., Ltd.（"Junshi Biosciences"）合作開發的抗PD-1單株抗體，目前為美國唯一核准用於治療這些適應症且商業化銷售的免疫檢查點抑制劑。本公司於2024年1月2日宣佈在美國啟動LOQTORZI的銷售。本公司、Junshi Biosciences及我們的生物藥品合作夥伴預計將透過多項現有及計畫中的臨牀研究進一步評估LOQTORZI。

本公司產品線包含兩項中階段臨牀候選藥物，目標為克服癌症中的免疫抵抗。我們計畫將其與LOQTORZI組合開發，並與擁有免疫活化或抗癌藥物的其他公司合作。我們的臨牀階段產品候選藥物casdozokitug（CHS-388，曾用名SRF388）為一種研究中的IL-27拮抗劑單株抗體，IL-27為一種免疫調節細胞激素，於某些癌症中過度表達，包括肝細胞癌、肺癌及腎細胞癌。casdozokitug於2020年10月獲美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）核准為治療肝細胞癌（"HCC"）的罕見疾病藥物。casdozokitug的主要適應症為一線治療肝細胞癌，目前正在進行一項隨機化第二期臨牀試驗，評估casdozokitug與toripalimab及bevacizumab組合用於肝細胞癌的治療（臨牀試驗資料庫識別碼# NCT06679985）。

我們的第二項臨牀階段產品候選藥物tagmokitug（CHS-114，曾用名SRF114）為一種去巖藻糖基化IgG1單株抗體，目標為CCR8，一種在腫瘤微環境（"TME"）中高度表達於調節性T細胞（"Treg cells"）上的化學趨化素受體。我們正在美國招募頭頸部鱗狀細胞癌（"HNSCC"）患者參與一項臨牀試驗，評估tagmokitug與LOQTORZI單獨或組合使用的安全性與藥動學（臨牀試驗資料庫識別碼# NCT05635643）。我們也已啟動一項多地區第一期b期臨牀試驗，評估tagmokitug與toripalimab及/或其他治療組合用於晚期實體腫瘤患者的治療，包括多個隊列，包括二線治療上消化道腺癌、二線治療食道鱗狀細胞癌（"ESCC"）、一線治療食道鱗狀細胞癌，以及評估四線以上治療結腸直腸癌的第二期a期隊列（臨牀試驗資料庫識別碼# NCT06657144）。我們也計畫進行一項臨牀試驗，評估tagmokitug與pasritamig（一種針對KLK2的T細胞活化雙特異性單株抗體）組合用於轉移性去勢抵抗性前列腺癌。
Coherus正在執行一項協調計畫，將LOQTORZI、casdozokitug及tagmokitug的生物製造流程轉移至美國本土。
本公司擁有科學專業知識、製造能力及美國本土的腫瘤學臨牀開發、法規事務、銷售及醫療事務經驗，這些經驗已支持LOQTORZI的商業化。我們預期將利用這些能力，持續推進我們的免疫腫瘤學產品線。
本公司在美國商業化LOQTORZI，並擁有全球開發及商業化casdozokitug及tagmokitug的權利。
本公司產品組合包含以下產品及產品候選藥物：
● LOQTORZI 是開發用以阻斷 PD-1 與其配體 PD-L1 和 PD-L2 之間的交互作用，透過與 PD-1 受體上的 FG 環結合。我們認為阻斷 PD-1 與 PD-L1 和 PD-L2 之間的交互作用，有助於促進免疫系統

的攻擊與殺死腫瘤細胞的能力。2023 年 10 月 27 日，我們宣佈 LOQTORZI 已獲美國食品藥物管理局核准，與順鉑及吉西他濱合用，用於治療接受治療的成人晚期或復發性局部晚期鼻咽癌，並作為單藥用於治療接受含鉑化療後疾病進展的成人晚期或復發性局部晚期鼻咽癌。LOQTORZI 是本公司與君實生物合作開發的抗 PD-1 抗體。我們於 2024 年 1 月 2 日宣佈在美國啟動 LOQTORZI 的上市。

2023 年 12 月 11 日，我們宣佈 NCCN 更新了鼻咽癌的臨牀實踐指引，將 LOQTORZI 列為成人晚期或復發性局部晚期鼻咽癌的首線治療選項，當與順鉑及吉西他濱合用時。2024 年 11 月 26 日，NCCN 進一步更新了鼻咽癌的臨牀實踐指引，明確指出 LOQTORZI 是唯一首線治療選項，用於治療接受含鉑化療後疾病進展的成人晚期或復發性局部晚期鼻咽癌，當與順鉑及吉西他濱合用時。指引也建議 LOQTORZI 單藥治療為後線治療的唯一首選治療方案。

LOQTORZI 的進一步評估預期透過本公司與合作夥伴進行的多項現有及計畫中的臨牀研究。我們有一項上市後承諾研究正在進行中，並在美國及加拿大地區招募病患，以進一步評估 toripalimab 與化療（順鉑及吉西他濱）合用在晚期鼻咽癌病患中的安全性與有效性（臨牀試驗.gov 識別碼# NCT06457503）。君實生物正在進行一項多地區第三期臨牀研究，評估 LOQTORZI 與其研究中的抗 BTLA 抗體合用在小細胞肺癌（LS-SCLC）的治療（臨牀試驗.gov 識別碼# NCT06095583）。INO Pharmaceuticals, Inc. 計畫進行一項隨機第三期臨牀研究，評估 INO-3112 與 toripalimab 在局部晚期、高風險 HPV16/18+ 或口咽鱗狀細胞癌中的治療效果。癌症研究協會正在評估 toripalimab 與 ENB Therapeutics 的研究中藥物 ENB-003 合用在第二期臨牀試驗「鉑耐藥高階別漿液性卵巢癌免疫治療平台研究（IPROC）」（臨牀試驗.gov 識別碼# NCT04918186）中，該試驗由加拿大癌症試驗組合作進行。STORM Therapeutics, Ltd. 正在評估其 METTL3 抑製劑 STC-15 與 LOQTORZI 合用在非小細胞肺癌、頭頸部鱗狀細胞癌、黑色素瘤及子宮內膜癌的治療中（臨牀試驗.gov 識別碼# NCT06975293）。2024 年 6 月 27 日，我們與 Apotex, Inc.（「Apotex」）簽訂了許可協議（「加拿大許可協議」），我們授予 Apotex 在加拿大（「加拿大許可協議」）獨家許可，以商業化 toripalimab。2025 年 10 月 23 日，加拿大衛生部核准 LOQTORZI 用於治療復發性無法手術切除或轉移性鼻咽癌。

● Casdozokitug（CHS-388，原為 SRF388）是一種研究中的重組人類 IgG1 單克隆抗體，針對 IL-27，一種免疫調節細胞激素或蛋白，該蛋白在某些癌症中過度表達，包括肝細胞、肺及腎細胞癌。IL-27 是巨噬細胞及抗原呈遞細胞分泌的細胞激素，其在抑制免疫系統方面具有重要的生理功能，如其能解決組織發炎。此外，IL-23 在懷孕期間高度表達，其表達與母胎耐受性相關。由於其免疫調節特性，抑制 IL-27 用以治療癌症是有根據的，因為這種方法會影響多種必須識別和攻擊腫瘤的免疫細胞的活性。Casdozokitug 於 2020 年 10 月獲美國食品藥物管理局授予罕見疾病藥物指定，用於治療肝細胞癌。Casdozokitug 目前正在進行一項持續的隨機第二期臨牀研究，評估 Casdozokitug 與 toripalimab 和 bevacizumab 合用在肝細胞癌中的治療效果（臨牀試驗.gov 識別碼# NCT06679985）。

● Tagmokitug（CHS-114，原為 SRF114）是一種研究中的人類去巖藻糖基化 IgG1 單克隆抗體，選擇性地針對 CCR8，一種在腫瘤微環境中調節 T 細胞（「Treg 細胞」）高度表達的趨化因子受體。Tagmokitug 設計為一種細胞毒抗體，透過抗體依賴性細胞毒性（「ADCC」）或抗體依賴性細胞吞噬作用（「ADCP」）或兩者，造成腫瘤內 Treg 細胞的減少，這些細胞是免疫抑制和耐受的重要調節者。Tagmokitug 在預臨牀模型中已顯示出抗腫瘤活性，作為單藥治療或與抗 PD-1 抗體合用。我們目前正在評估 Tagmokitug 與 toripalimab 合用在第二線頭頸部鱗狀細胞癌（HNSCC）的 Phase 1b 臨牀研究（臨牀試驗.gov 識別碼# NCT05635643）。我們也進行一項持續的 Phase 1b/2a 臨牀研究，評估 Tagmokitug 與 toripalimab 和/或其他治療合用在進展性實體腫瘤病患中的治療效果，第一組評估上消化道腺癌、食道鱗狀細胞癌及微satellite穩定（「MSS」）結腸癌（臨牀試驗.gov 識別碼# NCT06657144）。

paragraphs: 以下討論應配合本年度報告表 10-K（"表 10-K"）所包含之合併財務報表及其附註一併閱讀。本表 10-K，包括下列各節，包含根據聯邦證券法義義之向前看聲明。這些聲明受風險與不確定性影響，可能導致實際結果與事件與這些向前看聲明所表達或暗示者有重大差異。有關這些風險與不確定性的詳細討論，請參閱本表 10-K 第 1A 項之 "風險因素" 節。我們提醒讀者勿過度依賴這些向前看聲明，這些聲明僅反映管理階層於本表 10-K 之日期所作之分析。我們不負有更新向前看聲明之義務，這些聲明反映的是發生於本表 10-K 日期之後之事件或情況。

如下列所敘述，於 2025 年 4 月 11 日，我們出售 UDENYCA 商業業務，此為本公司生技類仿藥業務最後且最重要的資產處置，包含 UDENYCA、YUSIMRY 與 CIMERLI 品牌；因此，戰略轉變標準已達成。因此，生技類仿藥業務之資產、負債與營運結果已於本表 10-K 中歸類為已終止營運。因此，我們已回溯性地將所有生技類仿藥業務之資產、負債與營運結果歸類為已終止營運，並調整所有關於本公司生技類仿藥業務之資產、負債與營運結果之參考。

本公司為一家完整整合之商業階段創新腫瘤治療公司，已核准之新一代 programmed death receptor-1 抑制劑 LOQTORZI®（toripalimab-tpzi），以及包含兩項中階段臨牀候選藥物，目標為肝臟、頭頸部、結腸直腸及其他癌症之產品線。本公司策略為在鼻咽癌（NPC）中擴大 LOQTORZI 壽命銷售，並推進 LOQTORZI 新適應症之開發，與本公司產品線候選藥物以及合作夥伴共同使用，以驅動專利組合之銷售倍數與協同效益。於 2025 年 5 月 29 日，本公司將公司名稱自 "Coherus BioSciences, Inc." 改為 "Coherus Oncology, Inc."，以更符合本公司專注於專利創新免疫腫瘤藥物之獨家重點，此為近期完成生技類仿藥業務資產處置後，轉型專注於以創新藥物克服癌症免疫抵抗之結果。

本公司先前擁有 UDENYCA（pegfilgrastim-cbqv），於 2019 年 1 月在美國以預灌封注射器形式上市，隨後於 2023 年 5 月推出 UDENYCA 自動注射器形式，並於 2024 年 2 月推出 UDENYCA ONBODY。於 2024 年 12 月 2 日，本公司與 Intas 簽訂 UDENYCA 購買協議，根據協議，本公司同意將 UDENYCA 商業業務出售給 Intas。於 2025 年 4 月 11 日，本公司完成將 UDENYCA 商業業務出售給 Intas，獲取現金總計 483.4 百萬美元，包含 118.4 百萬美元之 UDENYCA 產品存貨。Intas 已指定 Accord 購買實體資產，包括產品存貨。本公司有資格獲得兩筆額外支付，每筆為 37.5 百萬美元（合稱 "Earnout Payments"）。第一筆支付為 Intas 若 UDENYCA 產品於 2025 年 7 月 1 日至 2026 年 9 月 30 日之連續四財季淨銷售額（根據 UDENYCA 購買協議之定義，"淨銷售額"）達或超過 300 百萬美元，則支付給本公司。第二筆支付為 Intas 若 UDENYCA 產品於 2025 年 7 月 1 日至 2027 年 3 月 31 日之連續四財季淨銷售額達或超過 350 百萬美元，則支付給本公司。
UDENYCA 銷售代表本公司生技類仿藥業務最後且最重要的資產處置，包含 UDENYCA、YUSIMRY 與 CIMERLI 品牌；因此，戰略轉變標準已達成，並於合併財務報表中包含已終止營運之呈現，適用所有已呈報期間。

於 2023 年 10 月 27 日，本公司宣佈 LOQTORZI 經美國食品藥物管理局核准，與卡鉑及吉西他濱合併使用，用於治療接受過 platinum 含藥物化療後疾病進展之成人晚期或復發性局部晚期鼻咽癌，且作為單一療法用於治療接受過 platinum 含藥物化療後疾病進展之成人復發性不可切除或轉移性鼻咽癌。LOQTORZI 為本公司與 Junshi Biosciences 合作開發之抗 PD-1 抗體，目前為美國唯一核准用於治療這些適應症且商業上可取得之免疫檢查點抑制劑。本公司於 2024 年 1 月 2 日宣佈在美國啟動 LOQTORZI 之銷售。本公司、Junshi Biosciences 及我們的生物藥品合作夥伴預期會透過多項現有及計畫中的臨牀研究進一步評估 LOQTORZI。
本公司擁有深厚的科學專業知識、經驗豐富且強大的製造技術，以及美國的腫瘤臨牀、法規、市場准入、銷售、關鍵客戶管理及醫療事務能力，這些能力已支持 LOQTORZI 之商業化。我們預期會進一步運用這些能力，以持續推進我們的免疫腫瘤藥物產品線。
本公司主要營運於美國，並與在其他國家營運之公司合作。

於 2024 年 12 月 2 日，本公司與 Intas 簽訂 UDENYCA 購買協議。根據 UDENYCA 購買協議的條款，並受其條件限制，本公司同意將 UDENYCA 商業業務出售給 Intas，交易金額為 483.4 百萬美元現金，包含 118.4 百萬美元的 UDENYCA 產品存貨，但需扣除於 UDENYCA 銷售交易關閉時交付的存貨低於存貨目標的數量。此外，本公司也有資格獲得兩筆額外的 Earnout 支付，每筆為 37.5 百萬美元，條件為在 UDENYCA 銷售交易關閉後特定期間內達到最低 UDENYCA 淨銷售額門檻。第一筆支付為 Intas 支付給本公司，若 UDENYCA 在 UDENYCA 銷售交易完成後的前五個完整會計年度內，連續四個會計季度的淨銷售額等於或高於 300 百萬美元；第二筆支付為 Intas 支付給本公司，若 UDENYCA 在 UDENYCA 銷售交易完成後的前七個完整會計年度內，連續四個會計季度的淨銷售額等於或高於 350 百萬美元。

本公司董事會一致批准並同意 UDENYCA 購買協議及該協議所預期的交易，包括 UDENYCA 銷售交易，認為此等交易符合本公司及其股東的最佳利益，並決議建議股東採納 UDENYCA 購買協議。於 2025 年 3 月 11 日，本公司股東在特別股東會議上投票批准 UDENYCA 銷售交易、UDENYCA 購買協議及其他預期的交易及相關附屬文件。該協議預期的交易於 2025 年 4 月 11 日完成。
本公司產品組合包含以下產品及產品候選品：

● LOQTORZI 是因其能阻斷 PD-1 與其配體 PD-L1 和 PD-L2 的互動，透過與 PD-1 受體上的 FG 環結合而開發。本公司認為阻斷 PD-1 與 PD-L1 和 PD-L2 的互動有助於促進免疫系統攻擊並殺死腫瘤細胞的能力。於 2023 年 10 月 27 日，本公司宣佈 LOQTORZI 已獲美國食品藥物管理局核准，與卡鉗鉑及吉西他濱合併使用，用於治療接受過化療後復發或轉移性局部晚期鼻咽癌成人患者，並作為單藥用於治療接受過含鉑化療後復發、無法手術切除或轉移性鼻咽癌成人患者。LOQTORZI 是本公司與 Junshi Biosciences 合作開發的抗 PD-1 抗體。本公司於 2024 年 1 月 2 日宣佈在美國推出 LOQTORZI。

於 2023 年 12 月 11 日，本公司宣佈 NCCN 更新了鼻咽癌的臨牀實踐指南，將 LOQTORZI 列為成人患者接受卡鉗鉑及吉西他濱合併使用時，治療轉移性或復發性局部晚期鼻咽癌的首選、一級治療選項。於 2024 年 11 月 26 日，NCCN 進一步更新了鼻咽癌的臨牀實踐指南，明確將 LOQTORZI 列為成人患者接受卡鉗鉑及吉西他濱合併使用時，治療轉移性或復發性局部晚期鼻咽癌的唯一首選一級治療選項。指南同時建議 LOQTORZI 單藥治療為後續治療線中，接受過含鉑治療後疾病進展患者的唯一首選治療。

本公司與合作夥伴預期將透過多項現有及計畫中的臨牀研究進一步評估 LOQTORZI。本公司目前有一項上市後承諾研究正在進行中，並在美國及加拿大地區招募患者，以進一步評估 toripalimab 與化療（卡鉗鉑及吉西他濱）合併使用在晚期鼻咽癌患者中的安全性與有效性（臨牀試驗資料庫識別碼# NCT06457503）。Junshi Biosciences 進行一項多地區第三期臨牀研究，評估 LOQTORZI 與其研究中的抗 BTLA 抗體合併使用在 LS-SCLC 患者中的治療效果（臨牀試驗資料庫識別碼# NCT06095583）。INOVIO Pharmaceuticals, Inc. 計畫進行一項隨機第三期臨牀研究，評估 INO-3112 與 toripalimab 在局部晚期、高風險 HPV16/18+ 口咽鱗狀細胞癌患者中的治療效果。Cancer Research Institute 正評估 toripalimab 與 ENB Therapeutics 的研究中藥物 ENB-003 合併使用，在其第二期臨牀試驗「免疫治療平台研究在含鉑治療後高階別卵巢癌（IPROC）」（臨牀試驗資料庫識別碼# NCT04918186）中進行，該試驗由加拿大癌症試驗組合作進行。STORM Therapeutics, Ltd. 正評估其 METTL3 抑製劑 STC-15 與 LOQTORZI 合併使用，在一項第一期/第二期臨牀試驗（臨牀試驗資料庫識別碼# NCT06975293）中，用於治療非小細胞肺癌、頭頸部鱗狀細胞癌、黑色素瘤及子宮內膜癌。於 2024 年 6 月 27 日，本公司與 Apotex 簽訂授權協議，根據協議，本公司授予 Apotex 加拿大授權協議。於 2025 年 10 月 23 日，加拿大衛生部核准 LOQTORZI 用於治療復發性無法手術切除或轉移性鼻咽癌。

任何本公司有意申請批准為原創新生物製劑之產品候選藥物，可能比預期更早面臨競爭。

本公司可能面臨管理員工人數變動之困難，特別是因資產處分、裁員及人員流動所導致之員工離職，可能幹擾本公司營運。
與依賴第三方相關的風險
本公司依賴 Junshi Biosciences 進行產品的商業化，若無法成功商業化，可能對本公司業務及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
與 UDENYCA 賣出後未來營運相關的風險
本公司無法保證將會收到 UDENYCA 購買協議下任一筆 earnout 支付。
與 UDENYCA TSA 相關的風險與不確定性，其中一項或數項可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果、現金流或股票價格造成重大不利影響。
與製造及供應鏈相關的風險
paragraphs: 投資於一家商業階段創新腫瘤學公司之普通股，包括一家擁有重大國際合作夥伴關係且有多項產品候選藥物正在開發之公司，是一項高度投機性行為，並涉及相當程度之風險。您應仔細考慮下列所描述之風險與不確定性，並配合本年度報告表10-K中所有其他資訊。若任何上述風險實現，將可能對本公司之業務、財務狀況、營運結果與前景造成重大且不利之影響。下列所描述之風險並非本公司所面臨之唯一風險。尚有其他未為本公司所知或目前認為不重要之風險與不確定性，亦可能對本公司之業務、財務狀況、營運結果與/或前景造成重大且不利之影響。
本公司擁有極有限之獲利歷史，且尚未持續維持獲利，亦可能無法再次獲利，且僅有一項產品已獲批准並上市銷售，且有多項產品候選藥物尚未獲批准仍處於開發階段。
自本公司成立以來，除某些因出售資產而產生獲利之期間及2020年與2019年外，本公司已產生大量營運虧損。本公司是否能在未來期間獲利，尚屬不確定，尤其在UDENYCA出售交易完成後，因研究與開發之費用高昂且風險極高。本公司未來之淨虧損或任何未來淨收入之金額，將部分取決於未來支出與未來產品銷售之金額，包括本公司現有產品或任何其他可能獲得監管批准之產品之銷售。
例如，截至2025年12月31日，本公司累計虧損為1.4十億美元。虧損與累計虧損主要係因本公司投入大量資源以商業化本公司產品，並識別、開發或取得本公司產品候選藥物，包括進行分析特性化、製程開發與製造、配方與臨牀研究，以及為這些業務提供一般及行政支援所致。
本公司已產生並預期將持續產生LOQTORZI之開發與商業化費用，LOQTORZI為本公司於2021年自Junshi Biosciences取得之anti-PD-1單株抗體，且本公司同意支付最高達90.0百萬美元以達成特定監管批准，以及最高達290.0百萬美元以達成特定銷售門檻。此產品之上市與未來為其他產品候選藥物進行臨牀開發之工作，將非常昂貴，並可能導致本公司持續經歷未來之淨虧損。

對於LOQTORZI，本公司唯一之商業產品，若本公司獲得任何其他產品候選藥物之監管批准，本公司未來之營收將取決於本公司產品候選藥物可能獲得批准之市場規模，以及本公司能否取得足夠之市場接受度、價格、第三方付款者之給付，以及本公司產品候選藥物在這些市場中之足夠市場佔有率，包括所有本公司已取得商業權利之產品候選藥物。然而，即使除本公司現有產品外，其他產品候選藥物亦獲得監管批准並商業化，本公司仍可能無法實現獲利。
